author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory: veterinarians grouped by the specialty they hold
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name (first then last). It lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster, and renders all specialties on one page with no paging.
acceptance_criteria: When the specialty directory is opened, every specialty is listed by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name (first name then last name, e.g. "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian who holds no specialty appears nowhere on the page — the page lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster.
All specialties appear together on a single page, with no paging (in contrast to the paginated veterinarian directory of REQ-VET-001).
A specialty held by no veterinarian still appears, listed with no veterinarians under it.
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, render in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
Listing veterinarians who hold no specialty anywhere on this page
notes: Inverse view of REQ-VET-001. The veterinarian directory paginates; this page deliberately does not. Read-only, per the product owner's in-scope decision; NG-2 is unchanged.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Inverse view of REQ-VET-001, entirely within the existing vet feature package and its established patterns (system-design.md Contracts + Persistence). No new module, pattern, or integration. The one addition is a name-ordered lookup repository for Specialty, which today has none (grep-confirmed: no SpecialtyRepository in src; IDE oracle not connected). It mirrors the PetTypeRepository precedent exactly. The new GET /specialties.html route lives in the existing VetController per the prd-entry file_targets. Read-only, so NG-2 is unchanged.
integration_points: New SpecialtyRepository in the vet package: mirror PetTypeRepository — an explicit name-ordered query (@Query("SELECT s FROM Specialty s ORDER BY s.name")) returning List<Specialty>. This is the enumeration source that makes empty specialties appear; do NOT derive the specialty set by inverting vet.getSpecialties(), which cannot see specialties held by no vet.

New GET /specialties.html handler in VetController: fetch all specialties (name-ordered, from SpecialtyRepository) as the OUTER loop, and all vets (vetRepository.findAll(), already @Cacheable) as the holder source; attach each vet to the specialties it holds; render templates/vets/specialtyList.html. No pagination (deliberate contrast to /vets.html).
Template renders each specialty by its stored name with its holders shown first-name then last-name; a specialty with no holders renders with an empty holder list.
Navigation link into the page (layout template) is out of this slice's file_targets — leave to a later slice unless the implementer finds the page otherwise unreachable in a test.

patterns.description: Name-ordered lookup repository via explicit @Query ORDER BY name — the exact shape SpecialtyRepository should copy so the specialty order is stable and lives in the query, not the controller.

Vet owns the @ManyToMany to Specialty (EAGER) via the vet_specialties join table; Specialty has no inverse mapping. This is why specialties must be enumerated independently, and why holder-membership is read off each Vet's specialties, not off Specialty.

risks.risk: Cross-persistence-context identity mismatch. SpecialtyRepository.findAll and vetRepository.findAll() run in separate read-only transactions (open-in-view is disabled and the vet result is cached), so the Specialty instances enumerated for the page are DIFFERENT objects from the Specialty instances inside each Vet's specialties set. NamedEntity/BaseEntity do not override equals, so identity-based grouping (contains / Set membership / == ) would place every vet under nothing and every specialty would render empty.
risks.mitigation: Group holders by a stable key, not object identity: build a Map keyed by specialty id (BaseEntity.getId()) — iterate vets, and for each vet.getSpecialties() append the vet to that specialty-id's holder list; then iterate the enumerated specialties and look up holders by id, defaulting to an empty list. A VetControllerTests case with a seeded holder-less specialty pins this.

risks.risk: Vets under a specialty render in arbitrary DB order — the acceptance criterion requires a stable order.
risks.mitigation: Sort each holder list deterministically (lastName then firstName) before adding to the model; specialties are already name-ordered by the repository query. Display remains first-name then last-name regardless of sort key.

notes: No ADR: this introduces no new pattern or hard-to-reverse trade-off — it is the PetTypeRepository lookup-repository pattern plus a route/template in the existing vet package. No system-design.md edit at triage time to preserve the doc's derived-from-working-tree provenance; doc-sync should wire REQ-SPEC-001 into the Contracts table (new SpecialtyRepository row; add REQ-SPEC-001 to the VetController, Vet, and Specialty rows) against the real code after the slice lands. Judgement on the PRD-author-derived criterion (empty specialty still appears): architecturally sound and load-bearing — it is what forces the independent specialty-enumeration read path above rather than the corner-cutting vet-list inversion. Dependency REQ-VET-001 is already implemented (VetController present); no conflict with NG-2 (read-only). No design-doc-autofix records to audit.

findings.description: PRD edge case 2 for REQ-SPEC-001 states 'Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order.' The ordering test specialtyDirectoryShouldOrderVeterinariansByLastNameThenFirstName covers only the second half — vet ordering under a specialty. There is no test that pins the order in which specialties themselves appear on the page. The production code delegates specialty ordering to SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties(), which per the design-block carries an ORDER BY s.name clause. Without a test, a future agent can drop that ORDER BY and no test will catch it. A test should be added that supplies specialties in non-alphabetical order from the stub and asserts they appear alphabetically in the rendered HTML, or that they appear in the same order as the repository stub returns them and that is the documented stable order.

The inline comment '// First name then last name, e.g. "Helen Leary".' in specialtyDirectoryShouldShowVeterinariansByFullName restates what the assertion assertThat(html).contains("Helen Leary") already says. Testing principles § Four-Phase Test Structure: 'never add prose that restates what the code already says. Phase comments, descriptive assertion messages on self-evident chains, and inline comments narrating obvious logic all violate this rule.' Remove the comment.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: SpecialtyListing is a pure data holder with two final fields and no identity — a value object per architecture-principles.md § Domain Core. The closed property requires all non-entity domain objects to be immutable and equal by value; the scoped exception covers only persistence-framework-instantiated types. The current class form provides neither value equality (no equals/hashCode) nor any immutability guarantee. Replace with a Java record: `record SpecialtyListing(String name, List<Vet> veterinarians)` with a compact constructor that wraps the list with List.copyOf(). No records exist in this codebase today (grep-confirmed; IDE not consulted), so this would be the first, but architecture-principles.md mandates the pattern for non-entity types.
findings.fix: Replace the static inner class with `record SpecialtyListing(String name, List<Vet> veterinarians) { SpecialtyListing { veterinarians = List.copyOf(veterinarians); } }` inside VetController. Update the constructor call sites in showSpecialtyList (the holders list is already sorted before being passed in, so List.copyOf is safe at that point). Remove getVeterinarians() and getName() — record accessors are veterinarians() and name().

findings.description: The SpecialtyListing constructor stores the caller-supplied List<Vet> without a defensive copy, and getVeterinarians() returns the internal ArrayList directly. A caller retaining the reference to the list passed at construction, or any code invoking getVeterinarians().add(vet), silently mutates the instance. architecture-principles.md § Domain Core (closed): 'Domain objects are immutable; collections use defensive copies.' The scoped exception does not cover view beans. This finding is superseded by the record conversion in the preceding finding if that fix is applied.
findings.fix: If not converting to a record: store List.copyOf(veterinarians) in the constructor field assignment, and return the stored field from getVeterinarians() without wrapping.

findings.description: showSpecialtyList builds its listings list with a for-each loop, and groupHoldersBySpecialtyId uses nested for-each loops. The code-quality checklist prefers stream pipelines for transformations. showSpecialtyList is a straightforward map from Specialty to SpecialtyListing readable as specialties.stream().map(...).toList(). groupHoldersBySpecialtyId is a multimap build expressible with Collectors.groupingBy. The Javadoc on groupHoldersBySpecialtyId explaining the getId() constraint must be preserved regardless of form.
findings.fix: In showSpecialtyList, replace the for-loop and mutable listings list with specialties.stream().map(s -> { List<Vet> h = new ArrayList<>(holdersBySpecialtyId.getOrDefault(s.getId(), List.of())); h.sort(Comparator.comparing(Vet::getLastName).thenComparing(Vet::getFirstName)); return new SpecialtyListing(s.getName(), h); }).toList(). In groupHoldersBySpecialtyId, consider Collectors.groupingBy on the flattened vet-specialty pairs; retain the Javadoc explaining getId() grouping.

approved_aspects: groupHoldersBySpecialtyId Javadoc precisely names the object-identity pitfall and its reason (separate persistence contexts, no equals on BaseEntity); a future editor will not undo getId() grouping without seeing why it exists
Deterministic vet sort order (last name then first name) is established at the call site and the Comparator is self-documenting

SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() documents the ordering guarantee in its Javadoc and enforces it in the JPQL query, making name-ordered rendering a repository contract rather than a caller convention
checkFormat passes; no formatting findings

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: showSpecialtyList calls holders.sort(...) on the list object returned by holdersBySpecialtyId.getOrDefault(...). When the key is present, getOrDefault returns the live map value, not a copy — the sort mutates the map's own internal list in place. This is safe given the current single-pass iteration but violates the 'no side effects in methods named as queries' principle and is a latent trap: any refactoring that re-queries the same key (e.g. multi-pass, reuse of the map) would receive an already-sorted list with no indication of why.
findings.fix: Replace the getOrDefault call with a copy: List<Vet> holders = new ArrayList<>(holdersBySpecialtyId.getOrDefault(specialty.getId(), List.of())); This makes the copy-then-sort pattern explicit and breaks the dependency on single-pass iteration being a correctness invariant.

approved_aspects: groupHoldersBySpecialtyId Javadoc explicitly explains the getId()-vs-object-identity constraint and the reason (separate persistence contexts, no equals on BaseEntity) — the design block's first constraint is legible cold

Deterministic sort by last-then-first-name is explicit at the call site (line 88) and pinned by the test specialtyDirectoryShouldOrderVeterinariansByLastNameThenFirstName — the design block's second constraint is legible cold
SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() enforces specialty ordering at the database level via JPQL ORDER BY, eliminating a second sort concern in the controller
Format check passed (checkFormat); naming and package placement are consistent with the vet package
Six tests cover the key behavioral contracts including the id-based grouping scenario with distinct Specialty instances

Rationale: the directory reads holder membership off each vet's @ManyToMany to Specialty (Vet owns that association; Specialty has no inverse), and it sources the vet set via vetRepository.findAll(). Both types genuinely serve REQ-SPEC-001, and the table already lists every participating type per requirement (REQ-PET-001 spans Pet, PetType, OwnerRepository, PetTypeRepository, controllers, formatter, validator; REQ-VIS-001 spans Owner, Visit, OwnerRepository). CONCURRENT CODE FINDINGS DO NOT WIDEN CONTRACTS SCOPE. The SpecialtyListing record-conversion and the showSpecialtyList/groupHoldersBySpecialtyId stream restructure are internal to VetController. SpecialtyListing is a controller-internal view holder living inside VetController.java, not a public file-owning top-level type — it gets no Contracts row whether it lands as a record or a class. ORDERING-GUARANTEE PLACEMENT (bears on the SpecialtyRepository row text). The test-reviewer correctly observed a @WebMvcTest with a stubbed repository cannot verify the ORDER BY s.name clause. author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD edge case 2 ('Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order') has two halves. The veterinarian-within-specialty half is pinned by theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderVeterinariansByLastNameThenFirstName using indexOf comparisons. The specialty-ordering half is pinned only at the DB level (SpecialtyRepositoryTests). No test at the controller or rendered-HTML level verifies that the controller preserves the repository's name-sorted sequence — that when findSpecialties() returns [dentistry, radiology, surgery], the rendered page shows dentistry before radiology before surgery. The stub in theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage coincidentally provides specialties already in alphabetical order (dentistry, radiology, surgery) and then only asserts contains(), so a controller that re-sorted or reversed the list would not be caught. The production code is trivially order-preserving (.stream().map(...).toList()), but the spec is not pinned at the rendered-page level.
findings.fix: Add indexOf-based ordering assertions to theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage (or a dedicated test): assertThat(html.indexOf("dentistry")).isLessThan(html.indexOf("radiology")); assertThat(html.indexOf("radiology")).isLessThan(html.indexOf("surgery")). The stub already provides non-ID-sorted input (id 3, 1, 2) so the test already exercises the controller's indifference to id ordering — only the order assertion is missing.

approved_aspects: theSpecialtiesShouldBeReturnedInNameOrder is non-vacuous: the H2 seed data (radiology, surgery, dentistry in insertion order) is not alphabetical — without ORDER BY, surgery before dentistry fails isSorted() independently of the test-added zoology/allergy entries. Dropping the JPQL ORDER BY clause would fail this test. The implementer's claim holds.

@DataJpaTest is the correct home for the ordering guarantee: the clause lives in the JPQL query, which only a real query execution can verify. A @WebMvcTest stub cannot observe it. Placing the test here is consistent with the design-block reasoning.

All six new test methods carry the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD naming convention (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowVeterinariansByFullName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtyWithNoVeterinarians, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderVeterinariansByLastNameThenFirstName). The pre-existing tests showVetListHtml and showResourcesVetList were not touched by this slice (git diff confirms no changes to their bodies), so the naming rule does not apply to them.

theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians still catches identity-based grouping after SpecialtyListing became a record: the test uses distinct Specialty instances sharing the same id for the directory-side vs the vet-held side. If groupHoldersBySpecialtyId used object identity instead of getId(), the lookup would produce empty lists and Helen Leary / Linda Douglas would not appear in the HTML. The record's List.copyOf compact constructor and value semantics do not affect this test's effectiveness.
Factory methods specialty(), vet(), and named() wrap all production-type construction in the new tests, satisfying the brief's factory-method rule for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward.
